result.question:
Research brief to de-risk and inform a build plan for TOPOLOGIX — a topological-data-analysis (TDA) platform for drug–protein interaction screening, with hERG cardiotoxicity prediction as the first validated MVP. The core scientific bet: persistent-homology features computed on the drug–protein interface ("Internuclear Persistence Contours") can beat cheap molecular descriptors at a real screening task. I need a fact-checked, citation-backed report covering:

1) STATE OF THE ART — persistent homology / TDA applied to molecular property and protein–ligand interaction prediction. Cover the key methods and their reported performance: Cang & Wei's persistent homology models, element-specific persistent homology (ESPH), TopologyNet, persistence images, persistence landscapes, atom-specific/interactive persistent homology for binding affinity (e.g. PDBbind), and any TDA work on toxicity. What representations and featurizations actually win, on what benchmarks, and at what accuracy/AUC. Where TDA genuinely adds signal beyond standard descriptors, and where it does NOT.

2) hERG CARDIOTOXICITY PREDICTION — the standard public benchmark datasets (e.g. Therapeutics Data Commons hERG / hERG_Karim, hERG Central, Cai et al., Wang et al.), their sizes and splits, and current state-of-the-art AUC/accuracy numbers. Critically: how well does a plain RDKit-descriptor + gradient-boosting (XGBoost) baseline do on these (the number our topological features must beat)? What is known about whether hERG blockade prediction needs 3D/structural information at all, vs being well-predicted from 2D ligand features. Availability and quality of hERG channel structures (cryo-EM, e.g. 5VA1 / 7CN1) for any structure-based approach.

3) GROUNDING THE NOVEL CONSTRUCTS — map three invented terms to the closest established mathematics so we can derive them rigorously: (a) "bipartite simplicial complex at a drug–protein interface" vs known interface/contact complexes, bipartite/relative persistent homology, witness complexes; (b) an "opposition-distance metric" between two atom sets vs known cross-distance / Vietoris–Rips on bipartite point clouds / distance-to-measure / DTM filtrations; (c) "persistence contours / surfaces" vs persistence images, landscapes, silhouettes, and persistence-surface vectorizations. What is genuinely unexplored space worth a novelty claim.

4) TOOLING & FEASIBILITY ON CPU — practical comparison of Ripser, GUDHI, giotto-tda, and Dionysus for the filtrations involved; computational cost of persistent homology at the scale of a drug + protein-pocket point cloud; whether this is tractable on a 4-vCPU CPU-only host; reproducibility pitfalls.

Deliver: what's proven, what's contested, the specific AUC numbers to target, the strongest grounding for each novel construct, and an explicit assessment of the central risk — that topological features may NOT beat a descriptor baseline on hERG — with the evidence on both sides.
result.summary: Persistent homology (PH) has a strong, peer-reviewed track record on protein-ligand binding-affinity tasks: Cang & Wei's element-specific persistent homology (ESPH), TopologyNet, and the MathDL lineage produced state-of-the-art PDBbind results and won 10 of 26 D3R Grand Challenge tasks, and the PATH/PATH+ "opposition distance" work directly grounds TOPOLOGIX's invented "opposition-distance metric" and "bipartite simplicial complex" constructs in published mathematics (Vietoris-Rips on a cross-distance/bipartite point cloud, with d_op originating in TNet-BP). However, the central scientific bet is at serious risk: on hERG specifically the evidence shows cheap 2D ligand features (fingerprints, RDKit/descriptors + gradient boosting) are already highly competitive-to-superior, structure/3D information adds interpretability and consensus value but NOT accuracy, and Wei's own topology-Laplacian model UNDERperformed a descriptor SVM on the standard Sato/Ogura external test (BACC 0.75 vs 0.80, SE 0.51 vs 0.67). Concrete targets: TDC hERG (648 cpds, scaffold split, AUROC) SOTA = MapLight+GNN 0.880; the RDKit2D+MLP baseline already hits 0.841; the realistic HTS-scale benchmark is the Sato et al. 291,219-molecule set (~28-29:1 imbalance, IC50<=10uM threshold) where a 22-descriptor XGBoost ensemble reaches ACC 0.87-0.90 but MCC only ~0.4. For grounding the third construct, "persistence contours/surfaces" map cleanly onto the Adams et al. persistence-image / persistent-surface 2D matrix vectorization (treatable as a CNN image), so the genuinely novel/unclaimed space is the combination — interface-restricted bipartite PH applied to toxicity (hERG) screening rather than binding affinity — not the underlying operators themselves.

findings.claim: PH/TDA has proven, state-of-the-art performance on protein-ligand binding affinity and pose prediction: Cang & Wei's ESPH/TopologyNet/MathDL beat conventional descriptor and scoring methods on PDBbind-scale data and won 10 of 26 D3R Grand Challenge tasks.
findings.evidence: ESPH ('multicomponent PH') retains element/atom-type information during topological simplification (Cang & Wei 2017/2018, PMID 28677268); TopologyNet (PLOS Comp Biol 2017) gave SOTA on PDBbind 2007 binding affinity and membrane/globular protein mutation stability; Nguyen, Cang & Wei (J Comput Aided Mol Des) ranked 1st in 10/26 D3R GC3 tasks; the original M2-channel MTF-SVM hit 96% drug-bound/unbound accuracy. Caveat: D3R-winning entries were hybrid ESPH + Multiscale Weighted Colored Graphs (MWCG), not pure PH, and 'outperforms existing methods' is relative to 2017-18 baselines — modern DL/Laplacian methods now match or edge ESPH.

findings.claim: The invented 'opposition-distance metric' and 'bipartite simplicial complex at a drug-protein interface' are grounded in published mathematics: opposition distance (infinite within-affiliation, Euclidean across protein/ligand) fed into a standard Vietoris-Rips filtration captures bipartite matching at multiple scales.
findings.evidence: PATH/PATH+ (PMC12226026, 2025): 'the opposition distance between a protein and a ligand atom is their Euclidean distance, while the opposition distance between atoms of the same affiliation is infinite,' and it 'works together with the construction of Vietoris-Rips complexes and persistent homology to capture bipartite matching of protein and ligand atoms at different scales.' Two important grounding caveats for TOPOLOGIX's novelty framing: (1) opposition distance is NOT original to PATH — PATH credits TNet-BP/TopologyNet (Cang & Wei) for introducing d_op; (2) no source uses the literal phrase 'bipartite simplicial complex' — the established construction is VR-on-a-cross-distance/bipartite-point-cloud. So the operators are published; only their interface-restricted application to toxicity screening is potentially novel.

findings.claim: The invented 'persistence contours/surfaces' construct maps onto the established Adams et al. persistence-image / persistent-surface vectorization: a 2D matrix derived from persistence diagrams (including multidimensional and element-specific PH) that can be treated directly as a CNN image.
findings.evidence: Pun, Xia & Lee survey (arXiv:1811.00252): 'The persistent surface is an example of 2D representation... these matrix representation can be treated as images and combined directly with convolution neural network (CNN),' with persistence images 'derived from persistent surface function (Adams et al., 2017).' ESPH binning produces a 2D image (spatial dimension x element-combination dimension) shown 'extremely useful in drug design.' Implication: 'persistence contours/surfaces' is a renaming of persistence-image/surface vectorization (alongside landscapes/silhouettes), so a novelty claim should rest on the application, not the representation.

findings.claim: The standard public hERG benchmarks and their sizes/splits are well-defined, giving concrete AUC targets to beat.
findings.evidence: TDC hERG (admet_group): 648 drugs, binary, AUROC, scaffold split. SOTA leaderboard = MapLight+GNN 0.880+/-0.002 (CFA 0.875, SimGCN 0.874, MapLight 0.871, ZairaChem 0.856). hERG_Karim: 13,445 drugs, binary, <10uM threshold (Karim et al. 2021 CardioTox). hERG Central: 306,893 drugs, two regression targets (% inhibition at 1uM and 10uM) + binary blockade. Note: leaderboards are mutable; numbers reflect current (2026) state.

findings.claim: A cheap 2D-ligand baseline (RDKit/descriptors + gradient boosting or MLP) is already very strong on hERG — this is the explicit number TOPOLOGIX's topological features must beat.
findings.evidence: On TDC hERG, RDKit2D+MLP (DeepPurpose) reaches AUROC 0.841+/-0.020 (rank ~7, within ~0.04 of the 0.880 SOTA). At HTS scale, the Sato et al. 291,219-molecule set (9,890 inhibitors / 281,329 non, ~28-29:1, IC50<=10uM) yields a 22-descriptor (from 4,298-pool) XGBoost ensemble of 29 base models at ACC 0.87-0.90, SE 0.83 / SP 0.91, but MCC only ~0.4 on the imbalanced set (up to 0.74 on balanced subsets). The descriptor target is therefore high accuracy/AUROC but a hard, imbalance-limited MCC ceiling — MCC is where a better representation could plausibly add value.

findings.claim: CENTRAL RISK — On hERG specifically, topological/structural features have NOT been shown to beat 2D-ligand descriptors; the strongest direct evidence shows topology underperforming a descriptor baseline.
findings.evidence: Direct head-to-head: Feng & Wei's topological-Laplacian AI model on the Sato/Ogura external test reached BACC 0.75 (SE 0.51, SP 0.99), UNDERperforming Ogura's descriptor SVM (BACC 0.80, SE 0.67) — though raw ACC (0.981 vs 0.984) and AUC (~0.963) were near-tied, so the gap is a sensitivity/imbalance effect on one benchmark. CToxPred benchmark (JCIM 2024): plain molecular fingerprints beat physicochemical descriptors AND graph-learned representations for hERG; corroborated by PMC12756696 where traditional fingerprints/descriptors beat 30 deep/graph representations and a 10-feature decision tree nearly matched the full model. This is the strongest evidence on the BEAR side of the risk.

findings.claim: hERG prediction does not require 3D/structural information to be competitive; structure-based (e.g. cryo-EM 5VA1) docking adds interpretability and consensus value, not superior accuracy.
findings.evidence: Creanza et al. (JCIM 2021, PMC9282647) benchmark study: best structure-based classifier (5VA1 induced-fit docking / MD with GLIDE docking score + interaction fingerprints) reaches AUC 0.85-0.86, described as 'comparable to ligand-based classifiers' (which independently reach AUC 0.93-0.95). Authors explicitly position structure-based methods as valuable for interpretability and consensus, not accuracy. Note: the broader claim 'hERG is predicted PURELY from 2D, structure not required at all' was REFUTED as overreach (0-3) — structure can still help domain coverage/interpretability; it just isn't required for competitive accuracy.

findings.claim: There is positive (but indirect) signal that PH carries information about representation quality: PH-derived topological descriptors of a representation's feature space correlate with ML generalization error better than competing modelability indices.
findings.evidence: TopoLearn (J Cheminformatics 2025, PMC12281805): PH variant achieves r=0.62 (p<0.001) correlation with generalization error vs ROGI-XD 0.28, RMODI -0.36, SARI -0.23. Confidence lowered to medium for the TOPOLOGIX bet because: (1) a sibling variant TopoLearn(C) scores HIGHER (r=0.68) with much of its edge from NON-topological controls (dimensionality, sample size); (2) scope is general molecular property prediction across 12 datasets, NOT drug-protein interfaces or hERG — applying it to TOPOLOGIX is an extrapolation.

findings.claim: Tooling/feasibility on a 4-vCPU CPU-only host — not directly evidenced by the verified claims.
findings.evidence: No claim about Ripser/GUDHI/giotto-tda/Dionysus performance, VR-complex cost at drug+pocket point-cloud scale, or CPU tractability survived verification. This brief section is UNANSWERED by the verified evidence and must be researched separately before committing the build plan. General domain knowledge (not verified here): Ripser is fastest for VR H0/H1 on small point clouds; pocket-restricted point clouds (hundreds of atoms, interface-only) keep VR tractable on CPU; GUDHI/giotto-tda offer the vectorizations (persistence images/landscapes); Dionysus is slower but flexible — treat as a hypothesis to validate, not a finding.

result.caveats: Time-sensitivity: TDC leaderboard numbers (MapLight+GNN 0.880; RDKit2D+MLP 0.841) are mutable and reflect the 2026 snapshot; verify before quoting in the build plan. Source-quality notes: claim [15] (topology underperforming descriptors on hERG) and [16] (fingerprints beating graph representations) were 2-1 votes — the dissent concerned scoping (single benchmark / single comparator; CToxPred compares fingerprints vs graph-LEARNED reps, not specifically vs PH/TDA), so they support the general thesis 'cheap 2D features can beat elaborate ones on hERG' but are NOT a direct PH-vs-descriptor hERG experiment — that exact experiment does not yet exist in the literature and is the crux the MVP must run. Attribution looseness across the Cang/Wei corpus: 'Cang & Wei' lumps Xia & Wei (2014 MTF), Cang et al. (2015 classification), and Cang & Wei (2017-18 ESPH/TopologyNet); D3R wins were MathDL/ESPH+MWCG hybrids, not pure PH. The 'opposition distance' originates in TNet-BP, not PATH. Three claims were refuted and excluded: PATH+ RMSE superiority over TNet-BP (1-2), the 'AUC clusters 0.80-0.95 so AUC is uninformative' framing (1-2), and 'hERG needs no structure at all' (0-3). The entire CPU-tooling/feasibility section (Ripser/GUDHI/giotto-tda/Dionysus, VR cost, 4-vCPU tractability, reproducibility pitfalls) has NO verified evidence and remains open.
openQuestions: Has anyone run the exact decisive experiment — interface/bipartite persistent-homology features vs an RDKit-descriptor + XGBoost baseline on a standard hERG split (TDC 648 or Sato 291k) — and what was the head-to-head MCC/AUROC? (No such study found; this is the MVP's core de-risking experiment.)

What is the actual CPU cost and memory footprint of Vietoris-Rips persistent homology (H0/H1/H2) on a combined drug + hERG-pocket interface point cloud across Ripser/GUDHI/giotto-tda/Dionysus, and is it tractable within a 48h sprint on a 4-vCPU host?

Does restricting the complex to the drug-protein INTERFACE (the 'Internuclear Persistence Contours' idea) add signal over whole-pocket ESPH, or does it discard information — i.e., is interface-restriction a feature or a bug for a ligand-property task like hERG that may not need the protein at all?

On the imbalanced HTS-scale hERG benchmark, can topological features move the metric that descriptors struggle with (MCC ~0.4) rather than the already-saturated ACC/AUROC, and is that the right success criterion to pre-register?

refuted.claim: PATH+ achieves an RMSE of 2.00 +/- 0.05 kcal/mol on the PDBbind v2020 refined set, outperforming the authors' TNet-BP implementation (2.31 +/- 0.11 kcal/mol) while using only 10 features versus TNet-BP's 14,472.

Across published hERG ML models, global accuracy and AUC cluster tightly in the 0.80-0.95 range with minimal variation, meaning headline ACC/AUC alone is uninformative and imbalance-sensitive metrics (MCC, F-measure, G-Mean, BACC) are needed to distinguish models. This sets the realistic AUC target band and warns against AUC-only claims.

hERG blockade is predicted purely from 2D ligand descriptors and fingerprints (physicochemical descriptors, ECFP, graph-based features); the entire study and the cited SOTA models are ligand-based with no protein structure, indicating structural/3D information is not required to reach competitive performance.
